subject: Hybrid SLA exception: split credits for uptime and latency (pilot)
messages:
From: Matthew Keller <matthew.keller@edgewave.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: hybrid SLA handling for EdgeWave pilot

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick pilot onboarding — things are shaping up well. Before we flip production traffic on, procurement here has asked for a slightly different SLA construct for the pilot period because we are routing some traffic through our on-prem connector. The ask is: can Redwood offer a hybrid exception for the first 3 months that separates uptime credits from latency credits?

Specifically:
- Baseline uptime target: 99.5% for the pilot (we can re-evaluate after 90 days)
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for our region (us-west)
- If uptime falls below baseline, EdgeWave requests a monthly credit proportional to downtime (standard availability credit)
- If latency breaches the p95 threshold, we request a separate monthly credit calculated against latency degradation so we don't double-credit the same incident

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) accept a dual-trigger credit model (separate uptime and latency buckets), and
2) provide a simple conversion table or formula we can include in the SOW for calculating the latency credit (example: X minutes of p95 breach = Y% of monthly committed spend).

Appreciate a quick sketch of the approach and any obvious caveats (maintenance windows, force majeure, regional connectivity issues). If useful we can jump on a 30-min call.

Best,
Matthew Keller
Head of Cloud Architecture
EdgeWave

--

Quick technical notes and a suggested formula from infra:

1) Measurement & exclusion windows- We should measure uptime as monthly aggregated service availability (total minutes available / total minutes in month). Maintenance windows (pre-scheduled + emergency maintenance with 24h notice) are excluded. Network outages originating in EdgeWave's on-prem connector should be an exclusion if the event is demonstrably inside their network.

2) Latency measurement- Recommend measuring latency at the customer route-level (us-west) with p95 computed across all successful responses. Important: only successful responses count toward p95 (failed requests attributed to availability).

3) Dual-trigger credit model (suggested):
- Uptime credit: credit_pct_uptime = min( (baseline_pct - observed_pct) * K_uptime, CAP_uptime )
  where baseline_pct = 99.5, observed_pct = monthly uptime, K_uptime = 200 (so a 0.1% shortfall => 20% credit), CAP_uptime = 20% monthly invoice (example numbers to iterate)

- Latency credit: convert latency breach into "latency-points" and then to credit_pct_latency. For example:
  * p95 > threshold by 0-100ms => 1 point per 1000 affected minutes
  * p95 > threshold by 100-300ms => 3 points per 1000 affected minutes
  * p95 > threshold by >300ms => 6 points per 1000 affected minutes
  Then: credit_pct_latency = min( (latency_points / latency_scale) * 100, CAP_latency )
  where latency_scale = 100 (example), CAP_latency = 10% monthly invoice.

4) Non-duplication rule- If an incident causes both availability and latency impact, crediting should apply to the single category that best reflects customer impact (availability first). In practice: when >= 50% of requests in the incident failed, treat as availability; otherwise treat as latency.

5) Reporting and evidence- We'll provide an automated monthly report with per-region uptime, p95 breakdown, incident timelines and raw samples. EdgeWave can open a support case to dispute.

These are starting points — Marissa / Laura / Kimberly to finalize caps and factors. If EdgeWave wants a formula tied directly to committed spend instead of monthly invoice we can adjust.

—Aditya
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: hybrid SLA handling for EdgeWave pilot

Matthew / team —

This looks reasonable for a pilot. A few contractual items we'd like to bake into the SOW / amendment:

1) Credit caps: aggregate monthly credit (uptime + latency) should be capped at 15% of the monthly committed spend for the pilot term.
2) Evidence & audit: Redwood will deliver a monthly metric pack (raw p95 samples, uptime timeline, incident logs). EdgeWave may request an independent audit within 60 days of a disputed credit (costs to be borne by the requester unless dispute upheld).
3) Exclusions: force majeure, third-party cloud provider maintenance (with notice), and EdgeWave-managed on-prem connector outages will be explicit carveouts.
4) Term: pilot exception applies for 90 days from go-live unless extended by mutual written agreement.
5) Remedies: credits only; no termination right or SLA-based refunds beyond the credit model during pilot.

I'll draft contract language for the amendment and attach to the Drive link Marissa mentioned. We should also include a simple example table (Illustrative) so procurement can see numbers against a $50k monthly commitment.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-16T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hybrid SLA handling for EdgeWave pilot

Matthew — thanks for the note and the constructive framing. Attached is an initial hybrid SLA draft (hybrid_sla_draft_v1.pdf) and a working credit table (monthly_credit_table.csv) that implements Aditya's dual-trigger approach and Laura's caps/exclusions. High-level summary in plain English:

- Uptime baseline: 99.5% for the 90-day pilot. Failure to meet baseline yields availability credits calculated as a function of the shortfall (see table). Cap on availability credits = 15% of monthly committed spend.
- Latency baseline: p95 <= 450ms (us-west). Latency breaches are converted into latency-points and then to a credit % (see table). Cap on latency credits = 10% of monthly committed spend.
- Non-duplication: if an incident results in widespread failures (>=50% failed requests during incident window), availability credit applies and latency credit is suppressed for that incident.
- Exclusions: explicit carveouts for on-prem connector outages (when indicated by EdgeWave-provided evidence), scheduled maintenance, and force majeure.
- Reporting: Redwood will publish an automated monthly metric pack and will honor a single evidence-driven audit request per quarter.

Next steps: please review the draft and the CSV, and let us know whether procurement wants the numeric caps softened (e.g., allow a 20% availability cap) or prefers the example tied to committed spend rather than invoice. If agreeable, I'd suggest a 30-minute call Thurs or Fri to finalize before we produce an amendment for signatures.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts (West)
Redwood Inference
